title: Migrate legacy checkpoint formats; streaming shard iterator; tokenizer adapter
creator: Diego Martínez
description: Summary: Clean up the model loading pipeline to reduce brittle format handling and long tail failures. This ticket covers three coordinated efforts: (1) migrating and normalizing support across legacy checkpoint manifests and new weight bundles, (2) implementing a streaming shard iterator to overlap IO/decompression with deserialization for large models, and (3) introducing a tokenizer adapter layer so runtime can accept both old tokenizer artifacts and new HF/third-party tokenizers without per-model hacks. Goal: make model load successful for >99% of onboarded models, reduce cold-start load latency by ~25-40% for 7B+ models, and eliminate several sources of OOM crashes observed in Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Loader accepts both legacy .ckpt manifest and new .weights.json bundles without per-model feature flags
Streaming shard iterator demonstrates >=25% wall-time overlap (IO+decompress vs deserialize) in benchmark harness for 13B model checkpoint (baseline measured)
Tokenizer adapter can map legacy tokenizers (vocab+merges) and HF tokenizers through a common interface; unit tests cover edge cases (unknown tokens, byte-level tokenizers)
No increase in unit-test flakes related to model load across CI (end-to-end load test passes in 95th percentile of runs)
Canary rollout plan executed on runtime-1.21 for hosted with 10% traffic and no increase in model load failures or memory OOMs over 48h
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Design doc (Confluence) with mapping of fields between legacy manifests and new bundle format; include explicit compat table for 'dtype', 'layout', 'shard_map' semantics
Phase 2: Implement MigrateManifest module that reads manifest, validates checksum, and emits normalized weight descriptor objects used internally
Phase 3: Build StreamingShardIterator with configurable chunk_size and prefetch_windows; uses dedicated IO threadpool to feed decompress+queue to main loader threads
Phase 4: TokenizerAdapter that exposes TokenizerV1 (legacy) and TokenizerV2 (HF) via the same runtime Tokenizer interface; add validation e2e tests against sample models
Phase 5: Integration: add feature-flag gated rollout (off by default) and automated rollback metrics (load_failure_rate, OOM_count, load_latency_p50/p95)
Benchmarks: add microbench for load_latency and memory footprint; compare baseline (current main) vs new pipeline for 3 model sizes (1.5B, 7B, 13B)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle weight ordering differences across formats may change model outputs. Mitigation: canonical checksum + per-layer shape verification + small inference regression tests against a golden prompt set
Risk: streaming IO could expose race conditions in KV cache warmup. Mitigation: start with read-only mode and conservative prefetch; add deterministic unit tests and race-detector runs

Risk: tokenizer normalization may slightly alter tokenization for edge-case inputs. Mitigation: include regression suite from evals-team and provide opt-out to keep legacy tokenization mapping for affected customers
Risk: rollout may reveal memory leaks. Mitigation: run extended soak on Dedicated staging and add memory budgets/limits with auto-fallback to non-streaming loader
